Task: kvlog-no-checksum
Editable paths (relative to the workspace root): server/

A small TCP key-value server (server/main.go) appends every PUT as a key=value line to data/kv.log, fsyncs and answers OK. On start it reads the whole log and rebuilds its in-memory map, discarding an incomplete last line. The storage layer occasionally returns data with a flipped bit on a read, while the stored bytes stay intact.

Observed on seed 1: after a restart the read of data/kv.log at disk read #1 returned a flipped bit at offset 95, the server started normally with a damaged map, and the client reported: acknowledged write lost: k16=v16, server now answers "NONE".

Expected: every PUT that returned OK must be readable after crashes and restarts, even when a read of the log is wrong once in a while.

Tools: list_files, read_file, write_file, edit_file for the workspace; run_seeds(seeds) to replay up to 4 seeds (integers from 0 to 1000; seed 1 reproduces the failure above) and see pass or fail with a reason and the end of the trace; submit() to finish.

name: read_file

content: The bug is that log lines carry no integrity check, so a flipped bit on read is silently accepted as data. I'll add a CRC32 to each line and make `open` read the log until two consecutive reads match before trusting it. A transient bad read then can't cause a bad map or a truncation.

content: Seed 4 shows the retry approach is too weak. Reads were corrupted many times in a row and the two-identical-reads check never succeeded within 50 attempts. I'll change the acceptance rule. A read is accepted when every complete line passes its checksum and the file ends cleanly on a newline. A torn tail (no final newline) is only trusted once two consecutive reads agree, because a flipped newline could otherwise make us truncate real data. Retries get a much larger budget.
